panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 6 panels (A, B, C, D, E1, E2). A: Case 2 chest radiograph from a pediatric Shwachman-Diamond syndrome cohort showing anterior rib end enlargement/costochondral thickening, a recognized skeletal manifestation. B: Case 4 chest radiograph from a pediatric Shwachman-Diamond syndrome cohort showing anterior rib end enlargement/costochondral thickening. C: Case 15 lower limb radiograph from a pediatric Shwachman-Diamond syndrome cohort showing bilateral femoral head epiphyseal dysplasia, a reported skeletal abnormality in this disease; the specific epiphyseal finding is not in the provided vocabulary. D: Case 17 lower limb radiograph from a pediatric Shwachman-Diamond syndrome cohort showing bilateral femoral head epiphyseal dysplasia; finding not represented in the vocabulary. E1: Case 5 sagittal chest CT from a pediatric Shwachman-Diamond syndrome cohort demonstrating a bony bridge connecting the posterior ends of the left 5th and 6th ribs, an unusual skeletal...

Skeletal and dental abnormalities, such as rib enlargement, femoral head dysplasia, and syndactyly, were observed in 63.6% (7/11) of cases (Figure 1). Renal abnormalities were noted in 45.4% (5/11), while cardiac ultrasound abnormalities were detected in 50% (7/14). Additionally, airway or bronchopulmonary dysplasia was observed in 11.8% (2/17) of patients. panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Facial photographs (frontal and lateral) of the younger brother with Shwachman-Diamond Syndrome (SDS); caption and article title attribute the patient to SDS and the in-text describes short stature and a convex-type lateral profile. Skin is visible and adequately lit, judged light. Eyes are redacted with black bars for anonymization. B: Intraoral photographs of the same SDS patient (Case 2) showing the maxillary and mandibular dental arches and occlusion; the in-text describes a V-shaped, spaced maxillary arch and excessive overjet (+5.0 mm) and overbite (+3.0 mm) in this SDS patient. No matching vocabulary finding key exists for the craniofacial/dental arch features, so they are recorded as proposed findings. Oral mucosa visible but no adequately lit skin for Fitzpatrick assessment.

in_text_mentions: On presentation, the patient’s body height and weight were 133.6 cm and 29.4 kg, respectively, and he also showed short stature. In the lateral facial view, he had a convex-type profile (Figure 5A). Intraorally, his overjet and overbite were +5.0 and +3.0 mm, respectively. His maxillary dental arch showed a V-shaped and spaced arch in the anterior part. His facial profile, excessive overjet, and maxillary dental arch were similar to those of his older brother. plate_findings.evidence: reduced thickness of the pancreas, particularly affecting the pancreas body and tail

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Axial T2-weighted abdominal MRI from a patient with Shwachman-Diamond syndrome, showing reduced pancreatic thickness. The article title and caption link the finding to Shwachman-Diamond syndrome, and the early-infancy presentation is atypical. B: Axial T2-weighted abdominal MRI from the same patient, showing reduced pancreatic thickness. Caption and article title support Shwachman-Diamond syndrome attribution. C: Fat-suppressed MRI sequence from the same Shwachman-Diamond syndrome patient, demonstrating no pancreatic lipomatosis, consistent with the atypical early-infancy imaging findings.
panels.attribution_text: Marsico et al. Atypical Findings of Shwachman-Diamond Syndrome in Early Infancy: A Diagnostic Challenge.. JPGN reports 2022. doi:10.1097/pg9.0000000000000165. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Abdominal MRI sequences. (A, B) Axial T2 weighted TSE MV sequences showing reduced thickness of the pancreas, particularly affecting the pancreas body and tail. (C) Axial T2 weighted TSE MV sequences with selective fat suppression (Spectral Presaturation with Inversion Recovery) at the same level showing no lipomatosis. MRI = magnetic resonance imaging; MV = multivane; TSE = Turbo-Spin-Echo.
in_text_mentions: An abdominal ultrasound (US) revealed a small-sized pancreas, with reduced thickness, particularly of the body and tail, abnormal echogenicity, and a “damaged” appearance (Figure 1). An abdominal MRI, including T2 weighted Turbo-Spin-Echo Multi-Vane sequences with selective fat suppression, confirmed the reduction of the pancreas parenchyma, without any fat infiltration or calcification (Figure 2).
